project_description.text: A 14,323 sqm vacant commercial lot with direct C6 Road frontage in Calzada–Tipas, Taguig, asked at ₱42,000/sqm (about ₱601.6M), tested as an 8,000 sqm leased dry warehouse.

company_developer.text: Mock client (fictional): a logistics holding company with three completed projects, buying to build and hold.

goals_objectives.text: Acquire, build in 12 months and lease to 3PL and e-commerce tenants; target 12% project IRR over a 10-year hold.

location_analysis.text: Strong access: C-6 widened to four lanes in 2017, linking Taytay to Bicutan, with the planned C6 Expressway adding upside. Taguig had 1.31M residents at the 2024 census.

market_analysis.text: Twelve nearby lot listings are asked at ₱20,000–70,000/sqm (median ₱35,000); the subject is ~20% above the median. Warehouse asking rents run ₱250–500/sqm/month.

technical_study.text: Zoning, title and site studies are not yet confirmed. Steel warehouses cost ₱14,000–22,000/sqm before slab, fire protection and site works.

socio_economic.text: Land in the C-5 and C-6 belts now competes with residential use; the BSP rate is 5.00% with a hike expected.

environmental.text: Lakeshore lowland with a flood history (Ondoy 2009). An elevation survey and flood check are needed; ₱20M site works is budgeted.

financial_projection.text: Total cost ₱834.8M. Stabilised net income about ₱35.0M a year (4.2% yield). Project IRR 2.5%; NPV −₱429.6M at 12%.

findings_recommendation.text: Land is the problem: the use supports ~₱9,900/sqm, or rents of ~₱1,000/sqm at the asking price. Test a higher-value use or negotiate.

conclusion.text: Not feasible as a warehouse at the asking price. The site's C6 frontage and size merit a test of retail or mixed-use, after zoning and flood checks.

key_risks.risk: Land price far above what warehouse rents support

next_steps: Request title, zoning and site studies from the listing broker
Commission an elevation survey and flood check
Test a retail or mixed-use concept on the same site
Benchmark an offer against the ₱35,000/sqm median

claims.text: The subject is a 14,323 sqm vacant commercial lot with direct C6 Road frontage in Calzada–Tipas, Taguig, asked at ₱42,000 per sqm.
Twelve comparable lot listings within about 1.2 km are asked at ₱20,000–₱70,000 per sqm, with a median of ₱35,000 per sqm.
Taguig warehouse asking rents range from about ₱250 to ₱500 per sqm per month; new builds near C6 are asked at ₱450–₱500.
Metro Manila warehouse rents can reach about ₱600 per sqm per month.
Basic steel-frame warehouses cost about ₱14,000–₱22,000 per sqm to build in 2026, excluding land, design, permits and site development.
Taguig had 1,308,085 residents at the 2024 census; Calzada-Tipas had 32,160 residents on 1.07 sq km.
The C-6 Laguna Lake Highway was widened to four lanes from Napindan to M.L. Quezon, opening 9 February 2017.
The 32.7 km C6 Expressway (₱45.29B, San Miguel Corp.) targeted its first phase within two to three years of February 2025.
Lowland areas along Laguna de Bay in Taguig are susceptible to flooding; the city was among the worst hit by Typhoon Ketsana (Ondoy) in 2009.
The BSP policy rate stood at 5.00% in early October 2026, with a further 25 bp hike expected.
At the asking price, the warehouse concept returns a project IRR of 2.5% against a 12% target.
The warehouse concept supports a land price of about ₱9,900 per sqm at a 12% project IRR.

blocks.text: This study tests whether a buyer should acquire the 14,323 sqm commercial lot on C6 Road in Calzada–Tipas, Taguig, at the current asking price of ₱42,000 per sqm (about ₱601.6M), and develop it as a leased dry-warehouse facility. The buyer's target is a 12% project IRR over a 10-year hold.

The warehouse concept was chosen because it is the first best-fit use named in the listing and the most common use advertised for nearby lots. The study follows the standard feasibility report structure, adding Methodology and Limitations and a Risk and Sensitivity section.

blocks.text: Twelve lot listings within about 1.2 km are asked at ₱20,000–₱70,000 per sqm, with a median of ₱35,000. Listings with C6 frontage or close C6 access sit at ₱30,000–₱50,000. At ₱42,000 the subject is asked about 20% above the median. Part of that premium reflects its direct C6 frontage and its size, since few parcels over 10,000 sqm are on offer.

blocks.text: Taguig warehouse asking rents run from about ₱250 per sqm per month for older stock to ₱450–₱500 for new builds near C6. Cushman & Wakefield puts the top of Metro Manila at about ₱600. Typical terms are a 3-year minimum, 3 months' advance and 3 months' deposit, with yearly escalation; one Tipas listing states 8%. Published guidance puts industrial escalation at 4–6%.

blocks.text: Construction cost: 2026 published ranges put basic steel-frame warehouses at ₱14,000–₱22,000 per sqm, excluding land, design, permits and site development. A heavy-duty slab adds ₱2,000–₱3,500 per sqm and sprinklers ₱800–₱1,500 per sqm. The model uses about ₱24,000 per sqm all-in for 8,000 sqm (₱192M), plus ₱20M for site works and fill, plus 10% soft costs.

Taguig had 1,308,085 residents at the 2024 census, the fifth most populous city in the Philippines. Calzada-Tipas itself had 32,160 residents on 1.07 sq km, and Calzada is one of the barangays with industrial areas.

Access is the site's strength. C-6, built along the Laguna de Bay shore as the Taguig Road Dike, was widened to four lanes from Napindan to M.L. Quezon in February 2017, cutting Taytay–Bicutan travel time by about half. The planned 32.7 km C6 Expressway (₱45.29B, San Miguel Corp.) targeted its first phase within two to three years of February 2025, and a San Pedro–C6 Laguna Lake Road would extend SLEX toward Taguig. Delivery timing is uncertain.

Land in the old C-5 and C-6 industrial belts is now competing with residential and mixed-use development, which Leechiu Property Consultants says is pushing warehouses out to Laguna, Cavite, Rizal and Bulacan.
Financing: the BSP policy rate stood at 5.00% in early October 2026, with a further 25 bp hike expected, so loan costs are rising rather than falling.

blocks.text: Nearby warehouses advertise "flood free" as a selling point, so flood resilience will affect rents and tenant demand. The model includes ₱20M for site works and fill; a survey may show more is needed.

Illustrative structure: the buyer acquires and holds the land through a project company, appoints a design-and-build contractor under a fixed-price contract, and retains an industrial leasing broker and a property manager. A pre-leasing commitment from an anchor tenant should come before the construction contract is signed.

blocks.title: Not feasible as a warehouse at the asking price
blocks.text: At ₱42,000 per sqm the warehouse concept returns about 2.5% project IRR, against a 12% target. Stabilised net income of about ₱35.0M a year is a 4.2% yield on the ₱834.8M total cost.

The land is the problem, not the building. This use supports a land price of about ₱9,900 per sqm (₱141.8M) at a 12% return. To work at the asking price, rents would need to be about ₱1,000 per sqm per month, roughly double the top of the Taguig market.
The asking price reflects higher-value uses and land banking along C6, not warehouse economics. That matches Leechiu's view that land in the C-5 and C-6 belts has become too expensive for warehouses.

items.result: The return gap is too large to close with leasing or cost savings alone

blocks.text: Not feasible. A leased warehouse cannot carry a ₱42,000 per sqm land price on this site: it reaches about 2.5% against the 12% target, and only works at about ₱9,900 per sqm. The site's C6 frontage and size are real advantages, so the next step is to test a higher-value use or negotiate the price, after confirming zoning, title and flood exposure.
Annex A lists the sources and Annex B the factual claims used in this report, each with its source.
